title: Fail-closed no-egress guard + local_only scope marking + egress_posture MCP tool + .well-known capability publication
priority_note: Highest-value story in the epic. #331 shipped agent autonomy over KB content while egress stayed uncontrolled AND undiscoverable - an agent can harvest a DNA file today with no supported way to check where it goes first. This story closes that, and it is the one capability that cannot be replaced by careful configuration.
background: Loopctl.Provider.Admission (lib/loopctl/provider/admission.ex, US-37.1 / GH #352) already sits immediately before every model-provider Req.post: anthropic.ex:118 guards :139, embedding_client.ex:91 and :101 guard :109 and :133. That makes it the correct chokepoint. CRITICALLY it is FAIL-OPEN BY DESIGN (admission.ex:81-97, fail_open/2 at :183) - it is a burst shedder whose job is to shed load without ever blocking legitimate traffic. An egress guard needs the OPPOSITE failure semantics. Fusing the two decisions would mean a Hammer or SystemConfig hiccup silently degrades the privacy guarantee to 'allow', turning a guarantee into a hope. The guard must therefore be a SEPARATE check at the same call sites that cannot inherit the fail-open path.

story.as_a: an agent about to harvest a user's private documents
story.i_want_to: mark the target scope local_only, have loopctl HARD-REFUSE any provider call that would send that data to a non-local endpoint, and query the instance's egress posture before I start
story.so_that: private data cannot leave the boundary by misconfiguration or by a wrong base_url, and I can verify locality first instead of trusting it

rationale: A privacy tier that depends on the operator configuring three endpoints correctly is not a guarantee. Fail-closed enforcement plus a machine-readable posture surface converts it into one an agent can verify - which is the only form that works on a platform with no UI.

acceptance_criteria.description: A local_only marking exists at tenant and project scope, settable via a new MCP tool + matching JSON API endpoint (no UI). Default off everywhere; the hosted instance behaves exactly as today until a scope opts in.

When a scope is local_only, every outbound model-provider call whose resolved endpoint is not classified local is refused with {:error, :egress_blocked} BEFORE the Req.post. The check is FAIL-CLOSED: if the endpoint cannot be classified, or if the classification machinery itself errors, the call is REFUSED. A test forces the classifier to raise and asserts the call is blocked, not admitted.

The guard is a SEPARATE decision from Provider.Admission's fail-open rate check, at the same call sites. Admission's fail_open/2 path can never admit a call that the egress guard would refuse. A test asserts that with the admission backend fully unavailable (fail-open triggered), a local_only scope with a non-local endpoint is still BLOCKED.

Local classification is explicit and operator-controlled: loopback and private-range hosts, plus a LOCAL_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST. api.openai.com and api.anthropic.com are never local. The allowlist is DEPLOYMENT-scoped and READ-ONLY to agents - it is the trust root, and an agent must never be able to widen its own allowlist through any tool or endpoint. A test asserts no API path mutates it.

egress_blocked degrades safely and legibly: the interactive path falls back like the existing circuit-open/rate-limited-local case (keyword search, never a 500); harvesting fails the ITEM with an agent-readable reason naming the scope and the offending endpoint, so the agent fixes config instead of retrying blindly. No data is sent in any path.

An egress_posture MCP tool + matching JSON endpoint reports: the resolved embedding and chat endpoints for the calling tenant, whether each is classified local, the deployment allowlist, and per-scope local_only status. Endpoints are shown; keys never are. This is how an agent verifies locality BEFORE harvesting.

The .well-known/loopctl discovery endpoint (US-26.0.4) publishes instance CAPABILITIES: supported embedding dimensions, whether tenant-supplied endpoints are permitted, and which tiers exist - so an agent can discover the instance's constraints BEFORE authenticating.

Hot-path cost is one cheap classification per provider call, with no additional network or DB round-trip on the common path (resolved config is already loaded). A benchmark or timing assertion documents it.

test_cases.name: local_only blocks a vendor endpoint, allows a local one
steps: attempt an embedding with base_url api.openai.com
attempt one with a loopback endpoint
expected_results: first: egress_blocked before any Req.post, nothing sent

test_cases.name: guard survives admission fail-open
preconditions: admission backend unavailable so fail_open/2 admits
expected_results: still blocked by the egress guard - fail-open must not leak into the privacy decision

test_cases.name: unclassifiable endpoint fails closed
preconditions: classifier forced to raise or return unknown
expected_results: reason states the endpoint could not be classified as local

test_cases.name: allowlist is not agent-writable
steps: attempt to modify the allowlist through every exposed tool and endpoint
expected_results: no path mutates it at any role

test_cases.name: posture report is complete and leaks nothing
preconditions: tenant with configured endpoints and keys
expected_results: endpoints, local classification, allowlist and per-scope local_only present
no key material anywhere in the payload

test_cases.name: interactive search degrades rather than 500s
preconditions: local_only scope with a non-local embedding endpoint
expected_results: keyword fallback with meta explaining egress_blocked

test_cases.name: capabilities discoverable pre-auth
expected_results: supported dimensions, tenant-endpoint support and tier list present

technical_notes: Place the guard at the same three call sites Admission already guards (anthropic.ex:118, embedding_client.ex:91,101) plus any new client from US-41.3 - but as its own with-clause, so the two failure modes never share a code path.

Classification must resolve the endpoint HOST, not the configured string, and must not be fooled by DNS pointing a public name at a private address or vice versa. Decide and document the resolution policy explicitly; the ingestion UrlGuard (content_ingestion_worker.ex:620-632) already faces this problem - reuse its approach rather than inventing a second one.

This story covers MODEL-PROVIDER egress only. Webhook delivery bypasses Admission entirely (webhooks/req_delivery.ex:43) and is handled in US-41.5 - the docs and the posture report must NOT claim total egress control until 41.5 lands.
egress_posture is a read tool and should be available at agent role: an agent must be able to check locality with the key it already has, or the whole verify-before-harvest workflow fails.
Record every egress_blocked decision in the audit log - US-41.7 turns these records into the custody claim.
